newsitem.title: USA: China's agricultural imports to keep growing--USDA.
newsitem.headline: China's agricultural imports to keep growing--USDA.

text.p: China will remain a key factor in global agricultural trade for the next several years, the Agriculture Department said Monday, foreseeing rapid growth in grain and oilseed purchases.
"Future demand trends in China's large and dynamic economy are particularly important to the long-term outlook," the department said in papers released at its annual Outlook Forum.
"China's coarse (feed) grain imports are projected to rise more than 10 percent annually," the department said.
East Asia, including China, was projected to expand soybean and soymeal imports by about eight percent a year.

"In China, although per capita wheat consumption is not expected to grow, imports are expected to expand about four percent annually as water shortages continue to inhibit yields," the department said.
